subject: Different estimates when fitting with se=FALSE or TRUE

messages.author: c2a477445d711b46
messages.subject: Different estimates when fitting with se=FALSE or TRUE
parts:
Hi there,

I am trying to fit what seem like simple pcount models where I have
only categorical covariates for abundance and detection. The only
complication is the fact that treatment (the covariate of interest) is
being added as covariate of both detection and abundance.

Because the fits take time, I decided to do them using se=FALSE as a
first pass for model selection using parboot to evaluate goodness of
fit. However, I wanted to check and see if the se's could be
estimated anyway, only to note that the means of the treatments were
quite different (see below). Does this mean that fitting the model
with se=FALSE and using parboot to evaluate GOF is problematic in this
case?

Thanks for your help in advance.
Leo

se=FALSE reports...
Abundance (log-scale):
Estimate SE z P(>|z|)
(Intercept) 1.2610 NA NA NA
treatment2 -0.0776 NA NA NA
treatment3 0.1473 NA NA NA
etc.
...

se=TRUE reports...
Abundance (log-scale):
Estimate SE z P(>|z|)
(Intercept) 2.7095 0.624 4.3401 1.42e-05
treatment2 -0.3138 NaN NaN NaN
treatment3 -0.0743 NaN NaN NaN
etc.
...

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Different estimates when fitting with se=FALSE or TRUE
parts:
Hi Pat,

I think you are referring to a different issue. Leo claimed that the estimates were different depending on the setting of the "se" argument. I don't see how this could happen, but I would really appreciate it if someone could send me a reproducible example.

Your issue of NaNs could be caused by many different factors, including parameter estimates near a boundary or a flat likelihood surface. Or poor starting values, etc...

Richard
